quick_skim.title: FunnelAL: Retrieve-then-Rank Active Learning for Single-Class Discovery
quick_skim.abstract: We present FunnelAL, a retrieve-then-rank active learning system for single-class discovery, which adapts the multi-stage funnel architecture of industrial recommender systems to data annotation. Large-scale supervised learning faces two challenges: efficiently finding relevant samples in a massive corpus, and distinguishing true positives from visually confusable negatives when embeddings do not cleanly separate classes. Conventional active learning offers a principled framework for reducing annotation cost, yet it treats sample selection as a single-stage process that addresses neither challenge efficiently. FunnelAL decomposes the problem into cascaded stages. Starting from a single positive and negative example, the system iterates through: (1) embedding-based retrieval scoring that narrows the corpus to a manageable candidate set; (2) a precision-triggered ranking stage that exploits a learned ranker (RankNet) while batch precision remains high, then automatically blends in committee-based exploration (QBC) once returns diminish; and (3) feedback from the annotator's labels that refines both stages in subsequent iterations. We evaluate on three diverse image classification benchmarks. With a perfect annotator, FunnelAL attains the best final F1 on all three benchmarks, the best annotation efficiency (first in AULC), and the fewest annotation rounds. The most recent single-class discovery methods (GAL, PF-MA) at best match its final quality, and only at consistently higher labeling cost. Under annotator labeling errors at realistic rates, FunnelAL remains first or statistically tied for first while classical uncertainty-based methods degrade two to three times faster. Our work provides a concrete bridge between multi-stage recommender systems and active learning.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: FunnelAL proposes a multi-stage retrieve-then-rank active learning system for single-class discovery, decomposing sample selection into cascaded stages to efficiently find relevant samples in massive corpora, offering transferable query strategies for active clustering.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: FunnelAL提出了一种检索-排序的主动学习系统，用于单类发现任务。它将传统单阶段样本选择分解为级联的检索和排序阶段，从少量正负例开始迭代，高效筛选海量数据中的相关样本。该方法展示了主动学习查询策略的改进设计，其原理可迁移至主动聚类场景中优化样本标注顺序。实验证明该系统在单类发现任务上显著降低了标注成本，同时保持了高精度。
